name: Asterid

items.name: Starlight Dependent
items.text: An asterid is mystically bonded to a single remote location with a good view of the open sky at night, most often a remote island, mountaintop, or open field. If they aren't in that location to see the sky at night on any given day, they become Drained 1, increasing the value by 1 for each night they miss, with the drained value increasing at sunrise each day. The drained value reduces by 1 only when they see the stars again. The asterid can perform a 24-hour ritual to bond to a new location.

items.name: Knowledge from the Stars
items.text:
Requirements It's currently night, and the asterid can see the sky

---
Effect The asterid looks to the stars for guidance and rolls a d20. Until the start of their next turn, they can use the result of their roll in place of making a check or saving throw. The asterid can't use Knowledge from the Stars again for 1 hour.

items.name: Starbeam
items.text: Effect The asterid launches a beam of starlight in a 120-foot line. Creatures in the line take 5d6 fire damage (DC 26 basic Reflex save save). Creatures who fail their save also become Dazzled for 1 round.

items.name: Starshine
items.text: An asterid's hair and skin always glow with soft starlight, producing 10 feet of dim light and ranging along the same blue-to-red spectrum as natural stars. This is a magical effect that can be suppressed by magical darkness or covered by, for example, a cloak, but never goes out entirely unless the nymph is killed.

text:
Asterids are nymphs of the stars, serene guardians of clear night skies and isolated pockets of the natural world far from the smog and light pollution of mortal cities. They spend their nights sitting in open fields or standing at the crests of high mountains, their heads tilted back to silently watch the stars go by. The rapturous, dreamy expressions asterids wear during their nightly observations have inspired countless works of art on the themes of beauty and longing.

As asterids are bound to general locations rather than specific natural features, they often must rely on alliances and friendships with other kinds of nymphs to find shelter. During the day, asterids generally end up sleeping in the tree-homes of dryads, beneath naiad ponds, or in the courts of their queens. This, alongside the asterids' generally quiet and gentle demeanor, leads many other nymphs to be somewhat protective of them, especially the asterid queens.

Mortals looking to establish an observatory can ask for no better location than one beloved by an asterid, though they would do well to approach such an endeavor with care and diplomacy. Those who come to the nymph with deference and respect the sanctity of the surrounding natural beauty may earn themselves a quiet but attentive guardian, eager to share their knowledge in exchange for the ability to more closely observe their beloved stars. Those who mar the natural world with excess construction or, worst of all, drown out the stars with excess light provoke the asterid's wrath and find their endeavor cursed with misfortune, if not destroyed entirely by the fury of the nymph's protective friends.
